name: x-change canonical vector brand library

x-change.description: Pulley wheel with five filled spokes on a shaft with a lifting hook, enclosed in a rounded capsule frame.

g-clef-pulley.description: Treble clef drawn as rigging: shackle, two multi-sheave pulley blocks, rope hatching, and a lifting hook.

fonts.note: No asset contains text. The brief's wordmark/lockup expectations were satisfied with mark-only compositions at differing clear space, because none of the source artwork contains lettering and inventing a wordmark would have meant designing new brand geometry.

audit_findings: logo.png is a different artwork from logo-orange/silver/slate.png, not a fourth colourway: it is the clef, while the others are the capsule pulley mark.
logo-orange.png, logo-silver.png, and logo-slate.png share pixel-identical alpha geometry.
favicon.svg contains no vector geometry; it embeds a raster <image> pointing at /images/logo-orange.png.
favicon.svg (capsule) and favicon.png (clef) depict different artwork, so the existing favicon set is internally inconsistent.
favicon.png is clipped at top and bottom (alpha bbox 132x192+30+0 in a 192x192 canvas).
No original vector source exists for either family, so all geometry here is reconstructed by tracing.

assets.usage: Dark (slate) treatment for light backgrounds and print on white.
assets.text_treatment: not applicable - artwork contains no text, so there is nothing to outline
assets.source_notes: Traced from logo-orange.png. The orange, silver, and slate PNGs were verified to have pixel-identical alpha geometry (0 differing pixels), so a single trace serves all three colourways and recolouring is exact.
assets.limitations: Geometry reconstructed by raster tracing (potrace 1.16) from an anti-aliased PNG at a 50% alpha threshold. Curves are approximations of the rasterised artwork, not the original design paths. Stroke weights are heavy (about 11% of artwork width), so the trace is stable at all sizes.

Highest-uncertainty regions: the dense multi-sheave arcs inside both pulley blocks, the rope hatching between them, and the overlapping hook linework, where adjacent strokes nearly merge at source resolution.
